veil-v2-hovers.detail: Light pressure (0.0174 m/s²) and Venus's gravity both point toward Venus; the shade falls with 0.0347 m/s² and reaches Venus in about 1 d.

veil-hovers.detail: At 1.11 × 10⁶ km sunward of Venus the residual is 0 m/s²; slats trim the small, slow drift of this unstable point by tilting.

second-law.detail: Pump work 2.92 × 10²⁷ J for 5.3 × 10²⁶ J of heat, at least the 9.0 × 10²⁶ J Carnot demands even if every joule left from 737 K, with the emitters as hot as 2,000 K.

exhaust-entropy.detail: The model charges pump work as if the hot side were at 2,000 K. Light at 0.91 MW/m² squeezed into a 0.4 µm band around 2.3 µm and a 25° cone counts as at least 16,000 K, 8.2 times hotter. Lifting a joule from the 737 K air into that light takes 12 times the work the budget charges.

graphite-for-caps.detail: 4.6 × 10¹⁷ kg of graphite by the end of sealing; the caps need 3.0 × 10¹⁷ kg.

ice-arrives.detail: Last launch 21 October 2035, a 1.15 yr transfer, last arrival 15 December 2036.

ring-energy-loop.detail: The Ring recovers 7.5 × 10¹⁹ W against the 6.7 × 10¹⁹ W the Railheads draw.

ring-net-force.detail: Catching half the Bricks eastbound and half westbound cancels the twist, not the force: 8.4 × 10¹⁵ N remains along Venus's orbital motion. An orbital ring has no stiff way to hand an in-plane force to the planet; its spare lift is 3.0 × 10¹³ N, 280 times too little.

ring-lowering-load.detail: Lowering 2.2 × 10¹² kg/s needs at least 4.7 × 10¹⁵ N; the rotor's spare lift is 3.0 × 10¹³ N, 150 times too little.

foundry-affords-veil.detail: The Foundry stands still for 9.8 d to build the 5.4 × 10¹¹ kg Veil, whose last parts leave Mercury on 16 September 2032; one doubling is 60 d.

foundry-size.detail: After 26 doublings the 6.7 × 10¹³ kg Foundry builds the 6.2 × 10¹³ kg Lattice in 80 d and the Ring in 13 d: both done 1653 days after landing, against 1687 with one doubling fewer and 1667 with one more.

foundry-builds-ring.detail: After the Lattice, the Foundry builds the 1.0 × 10¹³ kg Ring in 13 d; its last parts reach Venus on 19 October 2033, and the Ring must be complete on 31 December 2033.

aegis-structure.detail: The coil's field pulls on its winding with 1.2 × 10¹¹ N; holding it takes at least 2.0 × 10¹¹ kg of carbon fibre at full strength, 0.25 days of the full Foundry's output against the 60 d of one doubling.

frost-before-sealing.detail: The simulated Frost Towers finish on 22 August 2036; the last caps are sealed on 1 September 2036.

genesis-by-deadline.detail: Seeding waits for the oxygen (30 September 2036) and for the oceans to hold their pH (1 December 2036), so it begins on 1 December 2036; doubling every 1 d, the cells reach bloom density on 12 December 2036, against a deadline of 31 December 2036.

earth-like-by-deadline.detail: The day-by-day simulation reaches Earth-like conditions on 30 September 2036, 92 d before the 31 December 2036 deadline. The chimneys, not the power, set the pace on 56 d.

energy-closes.detail: Lattice supply 9.2 × 10²⁷ J against demand 8.4 × 10²⁷ J: 9.3% spare before the Ring's recovered energy, 34% once the Ring powers the Railheads.

energy-closes-with-ring.detail: The Lattice delivers 9.2 × 10²⁷ J against 6.1 × 10²⁷ J once the Ring powers the Railheads, and the Ring recovers 5.3 × 10²⁷ J against the 2.3 × 10²⁷ J of launches it pays for.
